title: Best AI Agent Platforms: 7 Platforms Compared

### **What Is an AI Agent Platform?**


An AI agent platform is software used to build, connect, deploy, monitor and control AI agents that perform work.


A real agent platform usually needs more than an LLM.


It may provide:


-


instructions or playbooks


-


company knowledge


-


memory and context


-


business-system integrations


-


tools and APIs


-


workflow execution


-


triggers


-


approvals


-


human escalation


-


testing


-


observability


-


governance


-


deployment controls


The critical distinction is **action** .


A chatbot may tell an employee:


> You should create a support ticket.


An AI agent may:


1.


Understand the issue


2.


Look up the customer


3.


Determine the correct process


4.


Create the ticket


5.


Add relevant context


6.


Route it to the correct team


7.


Tell the customer what happens next


8.


Escalate if the request falls outside its authority


That is why the best AI agent platform is not necessarily the platform with the most powerful language model.


The surrounding system matters just as much.


### **AI Agent Platform vs AI Agent Framework**


This distinction matters because current AI-agent comparisons frequently mix the two.


### **AI Agent Framework**


A framework such as LangGraph or CrewAI gives developers components for building agent logic.


Engineering teams may get detailed control over:


-


state


-


agent loops


-


tool calls


-


memory


-


orchestration


-


custom logic


But the company may still need to build or assemble other production layers itself.


### **AI Agent Platform**


A platform generally provides more of the environment needed to operate agents, such as:


-


deployment


-


connections


-


testing


-


permissions


-


monitoring


-


administration


-


human escalation


-


governance


The boundary is not perfect.


Some frameworks are becoming more platform-like, while many automation and enterprise-software vendors are adding increasingly sophisticated agent capabilities.


For buyers, the useful question is:


> **How much of the production agent stack do we want to build ourselves?**


### **How We Evaluated AI Agent Platforms**


For this comparison, six factors matter more than a flashy demo.


### **1. Can the Agent Take Real Actions?**


Can an agent:


-


update a CRM


-


create a ticket


-


trigger a workflow


-


retrieve account information


-


schedule something


-


modify an approved record


-


call another system


-


initiate another agent


An agent that can only answer questions is solving a smaller problem.


### **2. Can the Business Control How It Behaves?**


Enterprises need to define:


-


what the agent can access


-


which actions it can perform


-


when approval is required


-


when a human takes over


-


what policies govern execution


The more consequential the workflow, the more important these controls become.


### **3. Can It Use Enterprise Context?**


Useful agents need access to relevant context.


That may include:


-


company policies


-


CRM records


-


cases


-


tickets


-


product information


-


documents


-


customer history


-


operational state


The model alone does not contain this information.


### **4. Can You Test It Before Production?**


Agents behave in environments that contain ambiguity.


A serious platform should provide some way to test:


-


expected scenarios


-


edge cases


-


tool failures


-


escalation behavior


-


policy boundaries


before live customers or employees depend on it.


### **5. Can You Understand What Happened?**


Once agents take action, observability becomes important.


Teams should be able to investigate:


-


what the agent attempted


-


which information it used


-


which tools it called


-


what action occurred


-


whether it succeeded


-


where it failed


-


why a person became involved


### **6. Does It Fit the Existing Technology Stack?**


A technically strong agent platform can still be the wrong platform if it requires rebuilding the company's environment around it.


Integration fit matters.


### **1. Feather AI**


Feather is an enterprise AI agent platform built around customer conversations and operational workflows.


Its current platform is broader than its original voice-agent roots.


Every Feather agent can combine a playbook, knowledge base and tools. Businesses can describe agent behavior in plain English, while Feather compiles the instructions into a deterministic workflow graph.


That gives Feather a useful position between rigid workflow automation and unconstrained generative agents.


### **From Conversation to Completed Work**


Feather is particularly relevant when the agent has to interact with a customer and then do something.


For example:


> "I returned my order but still haven't received my refund."


The useful agent workflow is not simply:


**answer refund-policy question**


It may instead require:


**identify customer**


↓


**retrieve order**


↓


**check return status**


↓


**apply approved policy**


↓


**perform permitted action**


↓


**update system**


↓


**explain result**


↓


**escalate exception if necessary**


This is the kind of gap between conversation and operational completion that Feather has increasingly built its platform around.


Feather says its current platform combines agent configuration, knowledge, workflow instructions, communication channels, analytics, simulations, access controls, approvals, policy enforcement and audit trails.


### **Playbooks, Knowledge and Tools**


Feather agents use three core building blocks:


**Playbooks:** define how the agent should behave.


**Knowledge:** grounds the agent in company-controlled information.


**Tools:** let the agent interact with APIs and business systems.


The platform also supports model routing so different types of work can be sent to different models instead of forcing one model to handle every request.


### **Testing Before Deployment**


Feather supports mock tools and simulated testing so teams can rehearse agent behavior without triggering real system actions.


That is especially relevant when the agent has write access to business systems.


### **Why Consider Feather AI?**


-


Customer-facing agents


-


Operational agents


-


Plain-English configuration


-


Deterministic playbooks


-


Knowledge grounding


-


Business-system tools


-


API connectivity


-


Voice and digital interactions


-


Human handoffs


-


Model routing


-


Pre-production testing


-


Policy enforcement


-


Approvals


-


Audit trails


**Best suited to:** Companies that want AI agents to handle customer interactions and continue into controlled operational workflows rather than stopping at conversation or recommendation.


### **2. Salesforce Agentforce**


Salesforce Agentforce is an enterprise AI agent platform built directly into the Salesforce ecosystem.


Agentforce connects agents with Salesforce data, metadata, business logic and applications. It supports agents across use cases including customer service, sales, contact centers, field service, employee service and IT.


### **Salesforce Context as the Core Advantage**


Agentforce's biggest advantage is clear when Salesforce already sits at the center of the business.


An agent can use context from:


-


customer records


-


Data Cloud / Data 360


-


Salesforce workflows


-


service cases


-


opportunities


-


business logic


-


existing Salesforce actions


Agentforce also combines flexible AI reasoning with more deterministic controls through capabilities such as Agent Script.


### **Full Agent Lifecycle**


Salesforce describes Agentforce as supporting the complete lifecycle of building, testing, deploying, managing and orchestrating AI agents.


Current capabilities include:


-


Agent Builder


-


Agent Script


-


testing


-


observability


-


voice


-


MCP connectivity


-


multi-agent orchestration


### **Why Consider Salesforce Agentforce?**


-


Native Salesforce integration


-


CRM context


-


Customer 360 / Data 360


-


Agent Builder


-


Agent Script


-


Voice


-


Testing


-


Observability


-


Multi-agent orchestration


-


Large existing Salesforce ecosystem


**Best suited to:** Enterprises where Salesforce already owns a large part of customer data and operational workflow.


### **3. Microsoft Copilot Studio**


Microsoft Copilot Studio is Microsoft's platform for creating and managing AI agents, workflows and related business experiences.


Its biggest advantage is the surrounding Microsoft ecosystem.


Copilot Studio increasingly combines agent development with workflows, multi-agent coordination, real-time voice and connections across Microsoft's application environment.


### **Agents and Workflows Together**


Microsoft has been pushing Copilot Studio beyond simple conversational agents.


Recent releases have focused on:


-


multi-step business processes


-


computer-using agents


-


workflows


-


voice


-


multi-agent orchestration


-


connected applications


-


governance controls


This makes Copilot Studio increasingly relevant for organizations that already run important work through Microsoft 365, Power Platform and related Microsoft infrastructure.


### **Why Consider Microsoft Copilot Studio?**


-


Low-code agent building


-


Microsoft ecosystem integration


-


Business workflows


-


Multi-agent coordination


-


Real-time voice


-


Testing and evaluation


-


Governance


-


Microsoft 365 environment


-


Power Platform connections


**Best suited to:** Organizations deeply invested in Microsoft technology that want AI agents to become another part of the existing Microsoft workflow stack.


### **4. Google Gemini Enterprise**


Gemini Enterprise is Google's broader enterprise platform for agent development, deployment, orchestration and governance.


Google describes Gemini Enterprise as an end-to-end system for agents that can execute complex, multi-step work.


### **Google Cloud as the Agent Foundation**


Gemini Enterprise brings together:


-


Google's AI models


-


enterprise data


-


agent-development tools


-


secure deployment infrastructure


-


orchestration


-


governance


Google also introduced the Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform as the evolution of its enterprise agent-development environment.


A growing partner ecosystem also makes specialized third-party agents available through Gemini Enterprise.


### **Why Consider Google Gemini Enterprise?**


-


Gemini models


-


Enterprise agent development


-


Agent orchestration


-


Governance


-


Google Cloud integration


-


Enterprise data connections


-


Partner agents


-


Managed AI infrastructure


**Best suited to:** Organizations already committed to Google Cloud and Google's AI ecosystem that want a managed enterprise foundation for building and operating agents.


### **5. UiPath**


UiPath approaches AI agents from an automation-first background.


That gives it a different starting point from platforms built initially around chat or generative AI.


UiPath's agentic automation model combines agents with robots, workflows, integrations and people.


### **AI Agents Meet Existing Automation**


This becomes useful when an enterprise already has substantial automation.


A workflow may involve:


-


an AI agent reasoning about an exception


-


an existing robot performing a deterministic task


-


another system providing context


-


a person reviewing a consequential action


UiPath can coordinate those parts rather than expecting agents to replace every existing automation.


Recent UiPath updates include agent building, file analysis, human escalation routing, evaluation sets, guardrails and deployment through Orchestrator.


### **Why Consider UiPath?**


-


Agentic automation


-


RPA


-


Business-process automation


-


Human-in-the-loop workflows


-


Agent escalation


-


File analysis


-


Integrations


-


Evaluations


-


Guardrails


-


Enterprise orchestration


**Best suited to:** Large organizations with an existing automation estate that want agents to work alongside robots, workflows and employees.


### **6. Kore.ai**


Kore.ai offers a broad enterprise agent platform designed around building, governing and optimizing AI agents and multi-agent systems.


Its Artemis platform includes both visual and code-based development, structured agent definitions, governance and continuous optimization.


### **Governance as Part of the Agent Architecture**


Kore.ai puts considerable emphasis on defining agent behavior structurally.


Its Agent Blueprint Language is designed to define:


-


agent behavior


-


tools


-


guardrails


-


orchestration


-


handoffs


in a formal agent specification.


Kore.ai also offers a separate agent-management layer designed to manage and govern agents built across different frameworks and environments.


### **Build, Govern and Improve**


Kore.ai's current platform also includes Arch, which can take a business-language workflow and help design agents, tools, policies and handoffs.


Autoloop focuses on testing and improving agents against defined goals.


### **Why Consider Kore.ai?**


-


Enterprise agent building


-


Multi-agent systems


-


No-code, low-code and pro-code options


-


Structured agent definitions


-


Governance


-


Observability


-


Agent management


-


Cross-platform control


-


Testing


-


Continuous optimization


**Best suited to:** Large enterprises planning to operate substantial portfolios of AI agents and needing centralized governance and lifecycle management.


### **7. Make**


Make is an AI automation platform that has expanded its visual automation environment into AI agents.


Its biggest advantage is accessibility.


Teams can visually connect agents to thousands of business applications and combine AI decision-making with traditional automation.


### **Visual Agent Building**


Make AI Agents run inside Make's existing Scenario Builder.


Teams can:


-


define agent instructions


-


add tools


-


provide knowledge


-


connect workflows


-


test behavior


-


inspect tool usage


-


debug execution


in a visual environment.


Make also supports agent connections across thousands of applications, making it particularly useful for business teams automating work across SaaS tools.


### **Why Consider Make?**


-


Visual agent builder


-


Large integration ecosystem


-


Workflow automation


-


Agent tools


-


Knowledge


-


Transparent execution


-


Testing and debugging


-


MCP tools


-


Sub-agents


-


No-code accessibility


**Best suited to:** Business teams and automation builders that prioritize visual development and broad SaaS connectivity.
